title: Single-evidence policy cannot reuse older closure-identical evidence
commons_coordination: No Commons record filed. Owning layer is mncs-test coherence/Store history indexing.
observed_need: Coherence admits at most one evidence record per obligation (the current receipt file). When the semantic closure returns to a previously executed value (A PASS, B FAIL, C identical-to-A), the obligation re-executes even though vaulted evidence for that exact closure exists.
current_language_behavior: Demonstrated: PASS recorded, assertion broken (FAIL regression), assertion restored: the restore re-executes (correct, since the latest evidence is FAIL with a different closure) although PASS evidence for the identical closure exists in history. The system answers 'not current' instead of 'executed before with this closure'.
why_insufficient: Re-execution is sound but wasteful, and the report cannot distinguish 'never executed with these inputs' from 'executed with these exact inputs N revisions ago'. The latter is valuable regression-cycle signal.
minimal_reproducer: See docs/compiler-closure-contract.md fixtures note; scratch demo rev A (PASS) -> rev C (FAIL) -> rev D (closure == A): rev D executes rather than citing rev A.
desired_direction: Vault-indexed closure history: Store answers 'newest verdict for closure C' per obligation; native policy admits a history hit as a distinct reason (closure_recalled) with produced/current revision provenance and a regression/fixed transition against the latest evidence. Bound history depth explicitly.
workaround: Closed 2026-10-03: head-anchored lineage walk finds the newest vaulted evidence for the exact semantic world; native policy verifies admission on a second coherence pass; recalled reuse is distinct (recalled-closure source, recall note with head context, recalled transition). Projection and lineage stay head-anchored. Regression: test_closure_recall_reuses_identical_semantics, test_recall_requires_exact_semantics.
